docRequirement: headless.md:69 (§ Background tasks at exit) binds the non-interactive run's exit status to the signal that stopped it: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs `SessionEnd` hooks, and exits with code 143." 143 is the 128+SIGTERM convention, i.e. distinct from the 130 that a SIGINT (128+2) interrupt produces.
current: `nessy-general-agent run` is our `claude -p` analogue (`cmdRun`, apps/cli/src/index.ts:764; print mode declared at apps/cli/src/index.ts:782 via `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })`). It registers ONE handler for both signals and hard-codes a single exit code: `const onSignal = async () => { ... await cleanup(); process.exit(130) }` at apps/cli/src/index.ts:796-802, with `process.on('SIGINT', onSignal)` at :803 and `process.on('SIGTERM', onSignal)` at :804 (torn down at :861-862). The handler does perform the other clauses of the sentence: it cancels the turn (`client.invoke('sessions:cancel', sessionId)`, apps/cli/src/index.ts:798) and then `cleanup()` (:787-793) SIGTERMs the spawned headless server (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:118-121), whose own `shutdown` (packages/server/src/index.ts:367-374) runs `instance.stop()` -> `cleanupSessionManager` (packages/server/src/index.ts:270-277) -> `SessionManager.cleanup()` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:19138), where SessionEnd is run per managed session (SessionManager.ts:19160-19164). Only the exit number is wrong. `process.exit(130)` occurs exactly once in the whole source tree (`grep -ran 'process.exit(130)\|process.exit(143)' apps packages scripts` -> apps/cli/src/index.ts:801 only), and no test asserts a signal exit code (`grep -an 'SIGTERM|SIGINT|130|143' apps/cli/src/run.test.ts` -> no hits). Our own reference documents only the stream-event codes and has no signal row: docs/cli.md:131-133 (`error` 1, `complete` 0, `interrupted` 130).
divergence: The value, not the mechanism: SIGTERM must exit 143 and exits 130. Both signals share one handler with a constant exit code, so a supervisor cannot distinguish an operator Ctrl-C from an infrastructure shutdown. SIGINT's 130 is already correct and must stay. Registering ANY handler is what breaks it — Node/Bun's default SIGTERM disposition already yields 143; the explicit `process.exit(130)` overwrites the correct number. Positive control on this rig, both runtimes: a script using our exact pattern exits 130 on SIGTERM, the same script with the two `process.on` lines removed exits 143 (node 130/143, bun 130/143). The sentence's other three clauses (abort the turn, terminate the Bash process tree via the server teardown, run SessionEnd) are already satisfied through the cancel + child-SIGTERM path above and are NOT part of this divergence.

change.what: One-line behavioural fix: take the signal name the listener already receives and branch the exit code. `const onSignal = async (signal: NodeJS.Signals) => { ... await cleanup(); process.exit(signal === 'SIGTERM' ? 143 : 130) }`. Node and Bun both pass the signal name as the listener's first argument (verified on this rig: the handler logs `"SIGTERM"` under both runtimes), so the two existing `process.on(...)` registrations at :803-804 and the `process.off(...)` teardown at :861-862 stay byte-identical. Keep a comment naming the convention and the source: 128+signal — SIGINT 130, SIGTERM 143 (headless.md:69). If `@types/bun`'s `NodeJS.Signals` typing fights the async listener, widen the parameter to `(signal?: string)` rather than casting. Optional but recommended for testability: hoist the mapping into an exported pure helper next to `sendAndStream`, e.g. `export function signalExitCode(signal: string | undefined): number { return signal === 'SIGTERM' ? 143 : 130 }`, and call it from `onSignal` — `cmdRun` itself is not exported, so a unit test has no other seam.

Add the two-case table test over the exported `signalExitCode` helper: `SIGTERM` -> 143 (positive, the documented value) and `SIGINT` -> 130 (boundary, the value that must not regress). This file already imports named exports from `./index.ts` (apps/cli/src/run.test.ts:1-6), so no new harness. Do NOT attempt an end-to-end signal test here: `cmdRun` spawns a real server and needs an LLM connection, so a live kill test is out of the focused budget — state that in the plan rather than adding a flaky spawn.

Do not edit the existing `interrupted — exit code 130` row — that is the stream-event path (apps/cli/src/index.ts:538-541) and 130 is right for it. Add a separate signal row to the `run` section: SIGINT (Ctrl-C) exits 130 and SIGTERM exits 143, after cancelling the turn and running SessionEnd. This is the only doc surface that states CLI exit codes (`grep -ran 'exit code\|exit status' docs docs-site/content` finds nothing else outside plans/specs).

blastRadius: Confined to the CLI process boundary; no wire, schema or persistence surface, so none of AGENTS.md's risk triggers fire. (1) `onSignal` has exactly one enclosing caller, `cmdRun` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:764), itself dispatched once from `main` in the same file. (2) The other 130 in the CLI is a DIFFERENT path that must not move: `sendAndStream` sets `exitCode = 130` on the streamed `interrupted` event (apps/cli/src/index.ts:538-541), its doc comment says so (:446), and `cmdSend` exits with it (:591-593); collapsing the two paths onto one constant is exactly the bug. `sendAndStream` is covered by apps/cli/src/run.test.ts. (3) docs/cli.md:133 is the only user-facing statement of a CLI exit code and currently has no signal row. (4) apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:118-121 (`stop()` -> `proc.kill('SIGTERM')`, `await proc.exited`) is what makes SessionEnd run before we exit — unchanged, but it means the fix must keep `await cleanup()` BEFORE `process.exit`, or the doc's SessionEnd clause regresses while the exit code is being corrected. (5) Sibling that is deliberately out of scope: packages/server/src/index.ts:367-377, the long-lived `nessy-server` daemon, whose `shutdown` exits 0 for BOTH signals. headless.md:69 is scoped to `claude -p`, and the daemon has no `claude -p` analogue; changing it would also break packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts:195-203 ('shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM'). Name the surface in the commit so the daemon is not swept in. (6) No existing test asserts 130 or 143 anywhere in source (only unrelated hits inside the built apps/electron/dist/main.cjs bundle), so nothing goes red on the change.
userImpact: Observable today, on the first SIGTERM. Anyone running `nessy-general-agent run <prompt>` under a supervisor — `kill`, `systemd` stop, `docker stop`, a Kubernetes pod eviction, a GitLab CI job cancel or timeout, or an SDK host closing the session — gets exit status 130 instead of 143. Two concrete consequences: a wrapper written to the near-universal SIGTERM convention (`if [ $? -eq 143 ]`, or shell `$((128+15))`) never matches, so an infrastructure-initiated shutdown is reported as a generic failure; and a pipeline that treats 130 as 'the operator cancelled, do not alert' silently swallows a real timeout kill or eviction, because our 130 now means SIGINT, SIGTERM and the streamed `interrupted` event all at once. SIGINT/Ctrl-C behaviour is correct and unaffected.
